Beam diagram creator

Build a straight beam, place pinned and fixed supports and loads, and read its reactions, shear force, bending moment and deflection. Statically indeterminate beams such as fixed–fixed spans are solved by the stiffness method. Everything is calculated on this page, and the same model downloads as a NASTRAN deck.

Hand calculations

The same beam worked by hand, step by step, for every segment between consecutive supports and load points and at the point selected on the diagrams: reactions from equilibrium (or from compatibility when the beam is statically indeterminate), shear and moment by the method of sections, slope and deflection by double integration with the boundary and continuity conditions, then the bending stress and an equilibrium check. The stiffness solver is authoritative: every number below is its value, written as this page writes it, and the hand steps are a readable derivation of that same answer.

At the selected point x = 3000 mm

x = 3000 mm lies in segment 1 (x = 0 to 6000 mm), so s = x − 0 = 3000 mm.

V = 30000 − 10 (3000) = 0 N
M = 30000 (3000) − 5 (3000)2 = 4.5 × 107 N·mm
θ = 1EI(−9 × 1010 + 15000 (3000)2 − 1.667 (3000)3) = 0 rad
v = 1EI(−9 × 1010 (3000) + 5000 (3000)3 − 0.4167 (3000)4) = −12.66 mm
σ = |M| cI = 67.5 MPa

Method and reactions

Hand calculations: method, and how they relate to the solver

The direct stiffness solver is authoritative. These steps are a readable derivation of the same answer: every number shown is the solver's value at that step, written as this page writes it, and carrying the hand steps through reproduces it to the digits shown.

n = r − 2 = 2 − 2 = 0

The beam is statically determinate, so the reactions follow from equilibrium alone (sum of vertical forces and sum of moments).

  • Units: SI: N, mm, MPa. x in mm, measured from the left end.
  • Forces and distributed loads positive up; couples, slopes and support moments positive counter-clockwise.
  • V(x) is the sum of the upward forces left of the section; M(x) is positive when sagging; dM/dx = V, dV/dx = q and EI v′′ = M.
  • EI = 1.333 × 1013 N·mm2.

Reactions by equilibrium

Each load's vertical force and its moment about support 1 at x = 0 mm (counter-clockwise positive; a distributed load acts through its resultant):

Σj Fj = −60,000 N
Σj mj = −1.8 × 108 N·mm

Moments about support 1, where R1 has no arm:

R2 × 6000 + Σj mj = 0 ⇒ R2 = −−1.8 × 1086000 = 30,000 N

Vertical equilibrium then gives R1:

R1 + R2 + Σj Fj = 0 ⇒ R1 = −(−60,000) − 30,000 = 30,000 N

Shear, moment, slope and deflection by segment

Deflection and slope: double integration and boundary conditions

Integrate EI v′′ = M(x) twice. Each Macaulay term c⟨x − a⟩n integrates to c⟨x − a⟩n+1/(n+1), which keeps θ and v continuous at every support and load:

M(x) = −5 ⟨x⟩2 + 30000 ⟨x⟩
EI v(x) = −0.4167 ⟨x⟩4 + 5000 ⟨x⟩3 + C1 x + C2

Boundary conditions: v(0) = 0 (no deflection at support 1); v(6000) = 0 (no deflection at support 2).

With the reactions known, these give the two constants:

v(0) = 0: C2 = 0
v(6000) = 0: 6000 C1 + C2 = −5.4 × 1014
C1 = EI θ(0) = −9 × 1010 N·mm2, C2 = 0 N·mm3

So at the left end θ = −0.00675 rad and v = 0 mm; each segment below starts from the slope and deflection the previous one ends with.

Segment 1: x = 0 to 6000 mm

Cut the beam at x between 0 and 6000 mm and keep the part to the left of the cut, with s = x − 0 running from 0 to 6000 mm.

V(0+) = V(0−) + R1 = 0 + 30,000 = 30,000 N
M(0+) = M(0−) = 0 N·mm
q(s) = −10 N/mm
V(s) = V(0+) + ∫0s q ds = 30000 − 10 s
M(s) = M(0+) + ∫0s V ds = 30000 s − 5 s2
EI θ(s) = EI θ(0) + ∫0s M ds = −9 × 1010 + 15000 s2 − 1.667 s3
EI v(s) = EI v(0) + ∫0s θ EI ds = −9 × 1010 s + 5000 s3 − 0.4167 s4

Stress and equilibrium

Bending stress and the equilibrium check

The largest moment is 4.5×10⁷ N·mm at x = 3000 mm; the extreme fibre is c = 100 mm from the neutral axis.

σmax = |M|max cI = 4.5 × 107 × 1006.667 × 107 = 67.5 MPa

Equilibrium of the whole beam, loads and reactions together (moments about the left end):

ΣFy = Σi Ri + Σj Fj = 60,000 + (−60,000) ≈ 0
ΣM = Σi (Ri ai + Mi) + Σj mj = 1.8 × 108 + (−1.8 × 108) ≈ 0

Relative error of the two sums: 0.

NASTRAN deck

Download this beam as an MSC Nastran SOL 101 linear static bulk data file (.bdf). It encodes the same supports, loads, section and material the page solved, with every number in the units chosen above (SI: N, mm, MPa); a $ Units comment at the top of the deck names them.

Show the deck

  
Getting the .xdb results

  
  1. Save the deck, e.g. beam.bdf, on a machine with a licensed MSC Nastran installation.
  2. Run: nastran beam.bdf
  3. PARAM,POST,0 makes the run write beam.xdb next to beam.f06; open it in Patran (or another .xdb reader) to post-process.
  4. Compare DISPLACEMENT T2 (deflection) and R3 (slope, rad), and SPCFORCES T2 (reaction) and R3 (support moment), with this page in the same unit convention; the deck's $ Units comment names it. These are in basic coordinates and use the same signs.

  
The deck is generated from the same model the page solves and is checked by reading it back and re-solving it with the independent Python reference. This page does not run NASTRAN and does not produce an .xdb file itself.

  
What each card does
CardUse
GRIDOne grid per node along basic X; GRDSET sets PS=345 on every grid, permanently removing out-of-plane translation and rotations.
CBAROne bar per element, orientation vector X1,X2,X3 = 0,1,0 (element y = basic +Y).
PBARA, I1 (in-plane I), I2, J; K1/K2 blank = zero shear flexibility, matching Euler–Bernoulli.
MAT1E and ν; G left blank so NASTRAN derives it.
SPC1Set 1: one card for the pins (components 12) and one for the fixed supports (126), each listing its support grids.
FORCE / MOMENTLoad set 2: point forces along basic Y and couples about basic Z at grids.
PLOAD1Load set 2: TYPE=FY, SCALE=FR from 0 to 1 on each element under a distributed load, with the intensities at its ends.
PARAM,POST,0Asks MSC Nastran to write the Patran results database (.xdb) alongside the run.






  
Method, units and signs

  
Direct stiffness method with two-node Hermite beam elements between the supports and the beam ends. Point forces, couples and distributed loads inside each element enter as consistent nodal loads, which are the exact fixed-end actions for Euler–Bernoulli beams, so nodal deflections and reactions are exact and statically indeterminate supports need no special handling. Load points stay out of the stiffness matrix, so closely spaced loads do not degrade its conditioning, and there is no cap on the number of supports or loads. Shear and moment are then recovered exactly by statics from the loads and reactions, and deflection between nodes by integrating M/EI. Results are checked against an independent exact-arithmetic Python solver (Macaulay integration with compatibility conditions) on shared fixtures.

  
Sign conventions

  
  • x runs along the beam, positive to the right, measured from its left end or, when chosen, from mid-span (then from −L/2 to +L/2); +y is up.
  • Point forces and distributed loads are positive upward: enter downward loads as negative numbers.
  • Couples, rotations and support moments are positive counter-clockwise.
  • Shear V(x) is the sum of the upward forces to the left of the section.
  • Bending moment M(x) is positive when it sags the beam (tension on the bottom fibre); dM/dx = V and dV/dx = q.
  • At a point force V jumps by the force; at a couple C, M jumps by −C. Both one-sided values are reported.

  
Assumptions

  
  • Linear elastic, small displacement, static loading.
  • Euler–Bernoulli bending: plane sections stay plane and shear deformation is neglected.
  • Uniform prismatic section and one material along the whole beam.
  • Loads act in the plane of bending through the shear centre; no axial load, torsion, temperature or dynamics.
  • A pin restrains deflection; a fixed support restrains deflection and slope. Supports are rigid.
